`_json_safe()` treats `bytearray` as already-JSON-safe and returns it unchanged, but `gen_ai_json_dumps` only has a custom encoder for `bytes` (not `bytearray`). If a tool output contains a `bytearray`, span serialization will raise `TypeError` and can leak into the instrumented call path.

Convert `bytearray` to `bytes` (or otherwise normalize it) before returning so the util encoder can base64-encode it consistently.

threads.body: `_json_safe` currently falls back to `str(value)` for non-Mapping/non-Sequence types like `set`/`frozenset`. `str(set)` is not a stable/structured representation and can be order-dependent, which can make emitted span attributes non-deterministic across runs and harder to compare/debug. Consider adding explicit handling for `set`/`frozenset` (e.g., converting to a sorted list of JSON-safe items, or a deterministic string) before the final `str(value)` fallback.

Reworked this rather than adding a branch for `set`. `_json_safe` receives three fields. `output` is declared on two item types:

| field | declared type |
|---|---|
| `function_call.arguments` | `Required[str]` |
| `custom_tool_call.input` | `Required[str]` |
| `function_call_output.output` | `Required[Union[str, ResponseFunctionCallOutputItemListParam]]` |
| `custom_tool_call_output.output` | `Required[Union[str, Iterable[OutputOutputContentList]]]` |

The list variant holds `ResponseInputTextContentParam`, `ResponseInputImageContentParam` or `ResponseInputFileContentParam`, and every field on those three is a `str`, a `Literal`, `None`, or a nested `PromptCacheBreakpoint`. Note `input_file.file_data` is `Optional[str]`, a base64 string, so even binary payloads arrive as text.

So the reachable value space is: a string, a null, a list, a dict, or an SDK model that a caller replayed from `response.output`. `_json_safe` now handles the five reachable shapes and returns `None` for everything else, instead of falling through to `str(value)`.

`str(value)` can raise when `__str__` does, and handling every possible type here is not feasible. Those values are not valid input anyway: they fall outside the shape the SDK declares.

Import `ResponseCustomToolCall` in an isolated `try...except ImportError` block.

Responses API and `ResponseFunctionToolCall` were added in `openai 1.66.0`, while `ResponseCustomToolCall` was added in `openai 1.99.2`. On versions `1.66.0` through `1.99.1`, bundling this import raises `ImportError` and sets `Response` and `ResponseFunctionToolCall` to `None`, completely disabling Responses API instrumentation.

Consider also adding a test environment to the tox matrix for `openai 1.x` (e.g. `openai==1.66.0`) like we already do for `v2`.

In the Responses API ([API reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses/create#responses-create-input)), `input` is a flat list of items where each item has a `type`:
- `message`: standard user/system message with a `role`.
- `function_call` / `custom_tool_call`: tool call requested by the assistant.
- `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output`: tool execution result.

When mapping this flat list to `gen_ai.input.messages`:
1. `message` items map 1:1 to `InputMessage`.
2. Parallel tool calls are generated by the assistant in a single turn, but arrive as consecutive `function_call` / `custom_tool_call` items. These consecutive items should be merged into a single `InputMessage(role="assistant", parts=[...])`.
3. Tool outputs (`function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output`) should remain individual `InputMessage(role="tool", parts=[...])` messages, one per result.
